# PR #3752: Patch (part 5 of 6): card faces re-render only when their card changes

Closes #3609

## What changed

`Card`, `CardFace` and `MinionFace` were already memoised (#3478, #3633), so this PR adds no `React.memo` wrappers. They still redrew on every view for three reasons, and each is fixed here.

- **Fresh JSON on every view.** A view comes from `JSON.parse` (the wasm `viewFor`, a socket frame), so every card object was new even when the card hadn't changed. `sameCardProps` failed for every card and `useLiveFace` crossed into wasm for every card.
  - New `game/shareView.ts`: `Game` now calls `useSharedView(incoming)`. It replaces each subtree of `you`, `opponent` and `trades` that is deep-equal to the previous view's with the previous view's own object.
  - Arrays pair items by `instanceId`, so playing the first hand card keeps the later cards identical.
  - `events`, `pending` and `defs` are never shared. `newEventsSince` returns events by identity, and the sound director matches the runner's entries by it.
  - Nothing is shared across a change of viewer, which covers the hotseat hand-over.
  - The root is a new object whenever anything was shared, because `Game` and `lastSent` rely on "a new view is a new object".
- **One shared highlight.** `highlight` was compared by `Object.is`, so any selection redrew every card.
  - New `game/cardHighlight.ts` (`sameHighlightAt`), used through a new `"highlight"` case in `sameCardProps`. A card now compares only its own slice: its testids (own, `card-<id>`, `switch-<id>`) in the five sets, `outcomes` at its testid, its `activate-<id>…` controls in `legal`/`selected`/`glow`, and the hovered attack where it is the target or the attacker.
- **Hand hint row and drag ghost.**
  - `HandHints` took the whole `PlayerView`, which is new every view, so every own-hand card redrew. A new `HintView = Pick<PlayerView, "trades">` is memoised in `Hand`.
  - `DragGhost` called the uncached `liveFace` on every pointer move. It now uses `useLiveFace`.

Docs: `apps/web/README.md` has an updated Hand hints paragraph and a new "Card redraws" paragraph.

No Rust, spec, ruling or patch-fragment change, and nothing under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` or `.claude/`.

## Tests

- **New:** `shareView.test.ts` (16 tests), `cardHighlight.test.ts` (28 tests) and `Game.render.test.tsx` (6 tests, through `<Game>` with fresh-parsed views).
- **Counting method:** `marksOf` calls per card count drawings, and the wasm `face` calls are counted.
- **`Game.render.test.tsx`** pins the issue's acceptance bullets:
  - an unchanged fresh view draws no card;
  - one changed minion draws that minion only, and a played hand card draws no card that stayed;
  - selecting a hand card draws exactly the cards whose `data-legal`, `data-selected` or `data-glow` changed, and a strict subset of all cards;
  - pointer moves during a drag draw no card and make no face call;
  - pointer moves during an aim, including on and off a hovered target, draw no card.
- **Mutation check:** I reverted each fix in turn (sharing, highlight slice, `hintView`, ghost `useLiveFace`). Each revert failed its own tests.
- **Commands run, all green:**
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test`: 719 files, 12832 passed, 123 skipped.
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint` on the touched files.
  - `cargo fmt --check`.
  - `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok (`cardHighlight.ts` cites only the existing R3615000).
  - The related files (`Card.memo`, `Board.render`, `Hand`, `HandHints`, `Game`, `test/ux`) pass unchanged; I edited no existing test.
- **Not run:** the full e2e smoke suite. Only the frame probe ran, locally.

## Frame probe (#3605)

I ran `pnpm --dir e2e probe:frames -- --json` on this head. For the base (`f6b03c6ce8`), I built the same e2e client in a scratch worktree, which I removed afterwards. Headless Chrome on a shared runner, one run each.

These are the same within the probe's noise. Its frame granularity is about 16.7 ms and it ran once per side, so it does not show a before/after gain. The component-level counts above are the evidence for this change.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **No new `memo` on `Zone`, `Backrow`, `Board` or the hand's slot wrappers.** They are cheap shells that build `Card`s, and `Card`'s comparator is the gate. A wrapper would need the same comparator and repeat it. I rejected wrapping them.
- **Sharing lives in `Game`, not in `net.ts` or `wasm/index.ts`.** One call site covers the practice, hotseat and networked views. Sharing at each source was rejected because it would need the same previous-view state in three places.
- **Share only `you`, `opponent` and `trades`.** Sharing the whole view was rejected because of the identity-matched `events`.
- **A prefix match for Activate controls.** `activate-u1` also matches `activate-u10`, which only causes an extra redraw and never a stale one. I kept that over an exact per-ability list.
- **Accepted cost:** a change of `trades` redraws every own-hand card once.

## For the reviewer to look at twice

- **`sameHighlightAt` must list every read of a `Highlight` in a card's tree.** A missed read would leave a stale `data-*`. The header of `cardHighlight.ts` lists what is read now (`Card.tsx`, `ActivateControl.tsx`, `FieldBadges.tsx`), and the selection test compares the DOM attributes against the redraws.
- **Pile listings still recompute faces.** Graveyard and exile browse entries (`Board.tsx` `browseEntries`) call `listedFace` on every `Board` render. That is outside the issue's list (faces on the board, in the hand and on the ghost), so I left it. The `live`-call assertion in test 1 filters to cards on the board or in the hand for that reason. A follow-up could memoise the pile entries.
- **`useSharedView` writes a ref during render**, as `keptHighlight` does. A discarded concurrent render can only leave a ref holding the shared form of a view that was really received.

# #3609: Patch (part 5 of 6): card faces re-render only when their card changes
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

Part of #3604. The only memoised component in the client is `game/Log.tsx`'s `LogItem`. `Game.tsx` holds the view, the prompt, the drag and aim interaction and the animation queue's state, so every change to any of them re-renders `Board`, `Hand`, every `Card` and every `CardFace` / `MinionFace`. Each face also re-runs its keyword plan, art lookup, motion-slot hooks and fit measurement. During a drag or an aim, and while the animation queue drains, that is the whole board many times a second.

Make a face re-render only when what it draws changes:

- wrap `Card`, `CardFace`, `MinionFace` (and the per-card wrappers in `Board.tsx`, `Hand.tsx`, `Backrow.tsx` that need it) in `React.memo`;
- give them stable props: callbacks through `useCallback` or a ref (the `latest.current` pattern `DragLayer.tsx` already uses), derived objects through `useMemo`, and a face's card passed as the same object while it is unchanged (check how the view's cards arrive from `view_for` and the wasm module, and memo per card id + a cheap revision where the object is rebuilt every view);
- keep drag and aim position out of React state where it is only drawn (written to the DOM or a CSS property as `DragLayer` does).

Components still take a `PlayerView` and nothing else (CLAUDE.md, Architecture), and nothing here changes what the board shows.

### Acceptance

- A component test with React's `<Profiler>` (or a render counter): a view update that changes one minion's attack re-renders that minion's face and not the other faces on the board or in the hand.
- Moving the pointer during a drag or an aim re-renders no card face.
- Selecting a card re-renders only the faces whose selected or glow state changes.
- The whole web suite (`pnpm --dir apps/web test`), typecheck, and the e2e smoke pass unchanged.
- If part 1's probe has landed, the pull request quotes its combat numbers before and after.

1. **`game/shareView.ts` (new).** Header comment: a view arrives as fresh JSON, so equal subtrees are made identical to the previous view's.
   - `export function shareEqual<T>(prev: unknown, next: T): T` is a deep structural share:
     - `Object.is(prev, next)` returns `next`.
     - Arrays: if `prev` is not an array, return `next`.
       - Build `byId`, a `Map` from `instanceId` to item over `prev`'s items that are plain objects with a string `instanceId`.
       - For each `next[i]`, the partner is `byId.get(item.instanceId)` when `item` has a string `instanceId`, else `prev[i]`.
       - Map each item to `shareEqual(partner, item)`.
       - Return `prev` itself when the lengths match and every mapped item `=== prev[i]`; else return the mapped array.
       - Pairing by `instanceId` is what keeps the later hand cards identical when an earlier one is played.
     - Plain objects (non-null, non-array `typeof "object"`): if `prev` is not plain, return `next`.
       - Map each key of `next` through `shareEqual(prev[key], next[key])`.
       - Return `prev` when the key counts match, every key is an own key of `prev`, and every mapped value `=== prev[key]`; else return the new object in `next`'s key order.
     - Anything else (primitives) returns `next`.
   - `export function shareView(prev: PlayerView | null, next: PlayerView): PlayerView`:
     - If `prev === null` or `prev.viewer !== next.viewer`, return `next`. A hotseat hand-over must share nothing.
     - Otherwise compute `you = shareEqual(prev.you, next.you)` and `opponent = shareEqual(prev.opponent, next.opponent)`.
     - Compute `trades` only when `next.trades !== undefined`, as `shareEqual(prev.trades, next.trades)`.
     - If none of them is a different object from the one in `next`, return `next`.
     - Otherwise return `{ ...next, you, opponent }`, adding `trades` only when `next.trades !== undefined` (`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on).
     - Never share `events`: `newEventsSince` (animations.ts) returns events by identity so the sound director can match runner entries. Never share `pending`, `defs` or anything else. The root is always a new object when anything was shared, because `Game` compares `shown !== view` and `lastSent` relies on "a new view is a new object".
   - `export function useSharedView(incoming: PlayerView): PlayerView`:
     - Keep `useRef<{ incoming: PlayerView; shared: PlayerView } | null>(null)`.
     - During render, if the ref is null or `ref.current.incoming !== incoming`, set `ref.current = { incoming, shared: shareView(ref.current?.shared ?? null, incoming) }`.
